scope: docs/42-Pilot隔离运行监督器SDD.md backend implementability and consistency with docs/41 pilot_e2e journal

findings.title: Case ID width conflicts with catalog protocol
findings.detail: SDD 42 requires 256-bit IDs (64 lowercase hex characters); docs/41 and current journal accept 16 bytes / 32 lowercase hex characters. A supervisor-generated ID cannot be persisted without a protocol revision.
findings.required_action: Use the frozen 128-bit journal ID format or separately version and review the journal protocol before implementation.

findings.title: Context cancellation and bounded lock waits lack a contract
findings.detail: Public methods accept context and operations are required to be bounded, but the OS lock API and timeout behavior are unspecified. Existing pilotCatalogLock.Lock is context-free and its POSIX/Windows implementations block.
findings.required_action: Specify nonblocking lock acquisition with deadline/interrupt semantics, timeout errors, and poisoning behavior for uncertain unlock/sync outcomes.

findings.title: Verified filesystem handle adapter is not shaped as an implementable interface
findings.detail: The document names platform primitives but does not define the narrow root/relative-open/identity/sync/delete/close interfaces, capability probing, or supported OS matrix.
findings.required_action: Specify internal handle APIs and Linux/Windows capability matrix; keep case operations relative to verified handles.

findings.title: Supervisor and CaseHandle resource ownership under concurrent Close is ambiguous
findings.detail: CaseHandle.Close appears to close catalog-related handles while Supervisor.Close also owns closing all cases and supervisor resources. Concurrent close/use and partial-close ownership are undefined.
findings.required_action: Assign root/catalog/global lock to Supervisor and case lock/DB/sidecar/key to CaseHandle; define operation draining, close ordering, idempotency and poison semantics.

findings.title: SQLite driver open is not bound to the preverified OS handle
findings.detail: The SDD specifies mode=rw and post-open PRAGMA database_list validation but does not describe how the selected driver opens the file. The repository currently uses github.com/glebarez/sqlite, so path validation alone cannot establish that SQLite opened the already-verified file object.
findings.required_action: Specify exact DSN and connection-pool settings, validation order, file identity acquisition, and document the trusted-directory limitation unless a verified driver/VFS handle-binding path is proven.

positive_checks: pilot_e2e-only boundary and staged exclusion from production routes are clear
append-only durability and fail-closed behavior align with docs/41 journal invariants
Linux and Windows runtime acceptance is correctly required rather than cross-compilation alone
